title: A second 1000-level game

card.idea: Another game at about a thousand. Black’s fourth move puts the queen on e7, directly in front of her own king. It is a natural square and it defends a pawn, and it is the one square on the board where she can be pinned. Five moves later a rook on e1 takes her.
card.habit: Put a rook on the file the enemy queen is standing on.

explain.text: Black has just played 4...Qe7. It defends e5, it looks safe, and at this level it is played constantly. Nothing is wrong yet. But the queen is in front of her own king on a file that has not been opened, and neither of those things lasts.

The file is open. The queen on e7 cannot step off it without leaving her king in check, so she is no longer defending anything; and the knight on c6 is attacked by the pawn on d5. Move the knight and the rook takes the queen. Leave it and the pawn takes the knight.

challenges.prompt: Black’s queen is on e7, in front of her own king. Open the centre.
challenges.commentary: d4 is the break the whole set-up plays for. 6...exd4 7.cxd4 and the bishop on c5 had to move again — 7...Bb6 — because the recaptured pawn attacks it. The e-file is still shut by White’s own pawn on e4. That is temporary.
challenges.reason: d4 opens the centre and, after cxd4, wins a move against the bishop on c5.

hints.text: You already have a pawn on c3 supporting it.

challenges.prompt: Nothing is attacked and nothing is threatened. Put a rook where it will matter later.
challenges.commentary: Re1. The black queen is on e7 and her king on e8, and the only thing between them and the rook is White’s own pawn on e4. Nothing is threatened, which is exactly why this is easy to miss from the other side of the board. Black played 8...d5 — and opened the file himself.
challenges.reason: Re1 aims the rook at the black queen and king, with only White’s own pawn in the way.

hints.text: Which file are the black king and queen both standing on?

challenges.prompt: Black has just played 8...d5. Take, and then look down the e-file.
challenges.commentary: exd5 opens the file, and two things become true at once. The queen on e7 may not leave the file, because her king is behind her, so she is pinned; and the knight on c6 is attacked by the new pawn on d5. If the knight moves, Rxe7 wins the queen. If it stays, dxc6 wins the knight. There is no move that saves both.
challenges.reason: exd5 opens the e-file on a pinned queen and attacks the knight on c6 at the same time.

challenges.prompt: Black has moved the knight to a5, hitting your bishop. Answer the question that matters more.
challenges.commentary: Rxe7+. The knight ran and the queen could not, so the rook simply takes her. 10...Kxe7 wins the rook back, but the sum is a queen for a rook and a pawn, and the black king is standing on e7 in the middle of the board with plenty of game left.
challenges.reason: Rxe7+ takes the pinned queen. Kxe7 recaptures, and White has won a queen for a rook and a pawn.

hints.text: The queen cannot run. She never could.

challenges.prompt: The black king is on e7 and a knight sits on f6 in front of him. Pin it.
challenges.commentary: Bg5 pins the knight on f6 against the king on e7, and this one is absolute: the knight may not legally move, not even to capture. Black went material-hunting instead with 11...Nxc4, which hands White another move.
challenges.reason: Bg5 pins the knight on f6 to the king on e7, so it cannot legally move at all.

hints.text: A diagonal that runs g5, f6, e7.

challenges.prompt: Black has just taken your bishop on c4. Win a piece straight back, in the move order that gives him no say.
challenges.commentary: Qe2+ is check along the e-file at the king on e7, and from e2 the same queen looks at c4. Black has to answer the check first, and a piece comes back to White either way: the game went 12...Kf8 13.Qxc4. Check first, then count — a capture that arrives with check is one the opponent does not get to argue with.
challenges.reason: Qe2+ checks along the e-file and eyes c4 at the same time. Black must answer the check, and a piece comes back.

takeaway: A queen in front of her own king is not a defender, she is a target. Put your rook on that file before it opens, not after.
